new_symbol_range_suggestions.crowding_threshold_shift_strength: nonnegative; often 0 to a few dimensionless units so mismatch effects are modest for |N - crowding_memory| below carrying_capacity

derivation_notes: The parent assumed one blended crowding load determines density dependence, regardless of whether abundance is outrunning remembered crowding. Here the same blended load is multiplicatively modulated by normalized crowding mismatch, so positive mismatch intensifies effective crowding and negative mismatch relaxes it; the parent is recovered when crowding_threshold_shift_strength = 0 or along trajectories with N = crowding_memory.
change_summary: I refined the density-dependence law so the neutral-growth threshold shifts during transient crowding disequilibrium. This creates stronger suppression during overshoot-like increases and weaker suppression during declines at the same blended crowding load.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: A given effective crowding load causes the same growth suppression regardless of the current-versus-lagged crowding mismatch beyond its effect on the blend weights.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Transient overshoot or undershoot can make realized competitive damage depend on crowding disequilibrium itself, so the crowding threshold for zero net growth shifts with the sign and size of mismatch.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Set crowding_threshold_shift_strength = 0, or evaluate along N = crowding_memory, to recover the parent target law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: The net-growth zero occurs when a single effective crowding load, formed from the weighted average of current abundance and crowding memory, reaches carrying_capacity; this threshold does not depend on whether abundance is rising or falling except through the same lagged load.
response_change.child_relation: The crowding level at which net growth is neutral should shift with the direction and magnitude of recent abundance change, because rapidly increasing abundance can temporarily intensify crowding costs beyond what the same instantaneous load implies under slowly varying conditions.
response_change.observable_effect: At matched effective crowding load, trajectories with large positive N-crowding_memory show more negative dN_dt than trajectories with small mismatch, producing earlier growth suppression during overshoot episodes.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when |N-crowding_memory| is not negligible relative to carrying_capacity, especially during transients where crowding_memory lags current abundance; weak near quasi-steady tracking N≈crowding_memory.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate mismatch already changes the relation between effective crowding load and dN_dt; in holdout, larger transient mismatches amplify the same directional shift so suppression begins at lower load during rapid increases and relaxes during declines.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the mismatch-dependent threshold shift vanishes, e.g. zero strength of the new dependence or along trajectories with N=crowding_memory.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: mismatch-modulated density dependence under lagged crowding
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Transient overshoot or undershoot can make realized competitive damage depend on crowding disequilibrium itself, so the crowding threshold for zero net growth shifts with the sign and size of mismatch.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the effective crowding term now depends on the product of the parent load and a mismatch factor, creating a two-coordinate threshold surface over load and mismatch rather than one shared scalar threshold.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: A given effective crowding load causes the same growth suppression regardless of the current-versus-lagged crowding mismatch beyond its effect on the blend weights.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Crowding mismatch multiplicatively modulates the realized density-dependent load, shifting the neutral-growth threshold during transient overshoot or undershoot.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting crowding_threshold_shift_strength = 0 recovers the parent expression exactly; likewise the modulation is unity whenever N = crowding_memory.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: For equal effective_crowding_load values computed from the declared states, dN_dt is no longer unique: positive crowding_mismatch shifts growth downward and negative mismatch shifts it upward, with the contrast strongest when mismatch is appreciable relative to carrying_capacity and weakest near N≈crowding_memory.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this because the parent maps dN_dt only through one effective crowding load scalar. Any two observations with the same parent load must have the same predicted suppression there, whereas the child permits different dN_dt at that same load when crowding_mismatch differs; refitting parent parameters only moves the common threshold or curvature and cannot create mismatch-conditional separation across those conditions.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when |N-crowding_memory| is not negligible relative to carrying_capacity, especially during transients where crowding_memory lags current abundance; weak near quasi-steady tracking N≈crowding_memory.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, moderate mismatch already changes the relation between effective crowding load and dN_dt; in holdout, larger transient mismatches amplify the same directional shift so suppression begins at lower load during rapid increases and relaxes during declines.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the mismatch-dependent threshold shift vanishes, e.g. zero strength of the new dependence or along trajectories with N=crowding_memory.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes density dependence depends only on the level of blended crowding, not on whether the population is rapidly entering that crowding regime versus slowly varying through it.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: A given effective crowding load causes the same growth suppression regardless of the current-versus-lagged crowding mismatch beyond its effect on the blend weights.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Transient overshoot or undershoot can make realized competitive damage depend on crowding disequilibrium itself, so the crowding threshold for zero net growth shifts with the sign and size of mismatch.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-threshold assumption for density dependence. In the parent, once N, crowding_memory, crowding_sensitivity, and fixed parameters determine one effective crowding load, dN_dt is fixed; two states with the same load but different mismatch sign cannot differ except through that same scalar load. Scientifically, this omits transient overcompensation in crowding effects when abundance rises faster than the realized crowding environment can equilibrate. Vary the transient mismatch N-crowding_memory while holding intrinsic_growth_rate, carrying_capacity, crowding_exponent, and the effective crowding-load scale comparable. Then the child should predict stronger suppression for positive mismatch than the parent at the same blended load, especially during approach to carrying levels after rapid growth. This is observable under the actual ODE protocol because the supplied states already include both N and crowding_memory, and their mismatch naturally occurs from the stated initial conditions whenever adjustment is slower than abundance change. The effect is limited near equilibrium tracking where mismatch is small, and in that regime the parent remains a good approximation.

scenario_text: A closed population grows when rare but experiences progressively stronger crowding as abundance rises. The benchmark asks for the instantaneous rate of change in abundance along a continuous-time population trajectory. Birth and death conditions remain fixed, so density dependence is the only feedback controlling long-term abundance.
